rows.title_full: AN ACT PENALIZING THE UNJUSTIFIED INTERRUPTION OF SERVICE PROVIDED BY DISTRIBUTION UTILITIES AND TELECOMMUNICATIONS AND BROADCASTING ENTITIES
rows.abstract:
Mandates water and electric distribution utilities and telecommunications or broadcasting entities to address all customer complaints within one day from the receipt of the complaint - failure to address such complaint will make the concerned entity liable for a penalty payable to the customer.

Seeks to penalize these public utilities for service interruption that lasts for eight (8)  hours or more (for prepaid services or services with fixed regular fees); Entitles the affected customer to a refund or deduction on the bill.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 55 OF BATAS PAMBANSA BLG. 881, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE OMNIBUS ELECTION CODE, AS AMENDED, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Proposes that Sec. 55 of the Omnibus Election Code as amended, is hereby amended to read as follows:

Section 55. Office space - THE COMMISSION SHALL PROVIDE AN ACCESSIBLE AND SUITABLE PLACE FOR ITS FIELD OFFICERS AND THEIR STAFF, CHARGEABLE TO THE YEARLY APPROPRIATIONS OF THE COMMISSION.

Aims to remove from the hands of the local governments the power and duty to provide such office space to be consistent with and to be truly reflective of the constitutional independence that is due to the Commission.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING PROTECTION FROM LIABILITY TO VOLUNTEERS FOR ACTS OR OMISSIONS COMMITTED IN THE PERFORMANCE OF THEIR DUTIES DURING EMERGENCY SITUATIONS
rows.title_short: Providing Protection From Liability To Volunteers For Acts Or Omissions Committed In The Performance Of Their Duties During Emergency Situations
rows.abstract:
Seeks to provide liability protection for volunteers for harm caused by an act or commission if: 1.) the volunteer was acting in an emergency situation at the scene of an accident; 2.) the volunteer was property licensed, certified, or authorized by the appropriate authorities, either government entities or non-government organizations, for the activities undertaken in an emergency at the time of the act of omission; and 3.) the harm was not caused by willful or criminal misconduct, gross negligence, reckless misconduct, or a conscious, flagrant indifference to the rights or safety of the individual harmed by the volunteer.
Provides exceptions to the protection against liability of volunteers if: 1.) the misconduct constitutes a crime under the Revised Penal code or an offense in any special penal law; 2.) the misconduct was performed by the volunteer under the influence of intoxicating liquor or any dangerous drug at the time of the act or omission; 3.) the volunteers are from business organizations that employ volunteers for pecuniary purposes; and 4.) volunteers receive compensation for volunteering at a non-profit organization.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2020-03-10, transmitted to the Senate on 2020-03-11 and received by the Senate on 2020-03-11

rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE AMOUNT OF AUTHORIZED ELECTION CAMPAIGN EXPENSES OF CANDIDATES AND POLITICAL PARTIES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 13 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO.7166, ENTITLED, \"AN ACT PROVIDING FOR SYNCHRONIZED NATIONAL AND LOCAL ELECTIONS AND FOR ELECTORAL REFORMS, AUTHORIZING APPROPRIATIONS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES\"
rows.title_short: Increasing The Amount Of Authorized Election Campaign Expenses Of Candidates And Political Parties
rows.abstract:
Seeks to update the authorized expenses of candidates and political parties as follows: 1.For Candidates: Fifty Pesos (P50.00) for President, Vice-President and Senators; Thirty Pesos (P30.00) for other candidates for every voter currently registered in the constituency where they are seeking to be elected and have filed a certificate of candidacy for 2. For political parties: Fifty Pesos (P50.00) for their respective national candidates; and Thirty Pesos (P30.00) for local candidates for every voter.
Mandates the Commission on Elections, in consultation with the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, the NEDA and the PSA to adjust the amounts of authorized election campaign expenses every six years based on the inflation rate and the consumer price index.
